out.other_title: AI safety via debate: zero-sum self-play debate game judged by a human
out.rationale: The authors explicitly frame their Elo-accuracy trend as weak evidence for Irving et al.'s claim that debate at optimal play yields truth; the support is directional and, in the authors' words, only weak evidence.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether stronger debate play yields more truthful judge outcomes; holds for self-play debates judged by GPT-4-Turbo, not a human judge; the evidence is an empirical correlation, whereas Irving et al.'s optimal-play claim is stated by analogy to complexity theory; the evidence comes from one set of self-play questions, whereas Irving et al.'s claim covers any question in PSPACE given polynomial-time judges

text: The authors report a strong correlation between debaters' aggregate rating and judge accuracy in self-play debates (copies of the same model playing each other, judged by GPT-4-Turbo), so that as debaters are optimised against the unsupervised metric of win rate (judge preference), judge accuracy improves. They say this provides weak evidence that under optimal play debate produces truthful information (Irving et al., 2018).
title: Khan et al. find judge accuracy rises with debater rating, weak evidence for Irving et al.'s optimal-play claim
